items.title: George "Tex" Stephens Interview, 1996-08-23
items.q: He brought in Mahalia Jackson. Well, Mahalia had sung here before, but she was a big name at the time.

ctx.x: Because this was what you would call spiritual rejuvenation. A lot of people didn't understand what was happening with the blues, especially some of the white bands who just started picking up on the blues into the late 80s, that the blues really came out of the black church. And, well, prior to that, the sacrifices that blacks made were harmed from the soul because they paid so many dues. And then, as I talked with my old great uncles from way back when they spoke with their ancestors and relatives during the…
Did that cause the demise of that club? Because I don't think it...

items.title: George "Tex" Stephens Interview, 1996-01-10
items.q: we would rather identify with Mahalia Jackson or somebody else

ctx.x: TV? I guess like I used to like this show because I thought it was funny. I didn't have a great affinity to try to take it off the air but you had the NAACP and the Urban League and a certain element of people who had gravitated to schools and colleges and say well we kind of cultured now we don't need them kind of people no more. Well I don't feel that we could throw those people out because they still are part of the entertainment history of this nation and I think they should be seen and they should be heard…
I agree with you 100% so all in all
